title: Not Feeling Well
subtitle: Four scenes about small health problems
review: Written by Claude: check the English lines, the notes and the questions. No Burmese yet.
intro: A cold that might be the end, a headache that needs a quiet room, a back hurt by a sock and a recovery timed to the minute: four short scenes between Emma and Lucas. Listen for I have a…, for the advice with you should, and for how you say that you feel better.

lines.note: The everyday way to say you are sick. Also: I'm not feeling well.
= What's wrong? Answer with the problem: I have a…

lines.text: I have a sore throat. And a runny nose. And a cough.
lines.note: Sore: it hurts. Runny nose: water keeps coming from it. Cough sounds like koff.
A cold, with a. I have cold is wrong: I'm cold means the room is cold.

lines.text: I think it's more serious than that.
lines.note: Serious: bad, maybe dangerous. More serious than…
A fever: your body is too hot.
37.2 in Celsius. The dot is said point. Normal is about 37; a fever starts around 38.

lines.text: That's not a fever. That's a person.
lines.note: She means: 37.2 is what every healthy person has.

lines.text: Tell my mother I loved her.
lines.note: Tell + person + the message. Loved, in the past: he talks as if he were already gone.

lines.text: Tell her yourself. She's calling at six.
lines.note: Yourself: you, not me. She's calling at six: a plan for later today.
Headache, stomachache, toothache: one word, with -ache. It sounds like ake.
= When did it start?
Since + the time it started: since Monday, since yesterday.
Have you tried + verb-ing: a gentle way to give advice.
Short for Have you tried fresh air? Fresh air: the air outside.

lines.text: You should lie down in a quiet room.
lines.note: You should + verb: advice. Lie down: rest flat on a bed or a sofa.

lines.text: Good idea. Which room will you be in?
lines.note: She wants the room without Lucas in it.
Ow! or Ouch!: what you say when something hurts.
Asks about something that is over: a fall, an accident.

lines.text: I picked something up. Something heavy.
lines.note: Pick up: take from the floor. Heavy: hard to lift.
One, not a: she can't believe the number.
Wet: with water in it. The opposite is dry.
See a doctor: go for help. Not: meet a doctor.
= What can I say to him?

lines.text: The truth. He needs a laugh too.
lines.note: The truth: what really happened. Need a laugh: need something funny.
Also: How are you feeling?

lines.text: A little better. But I'm still very weak.
lines.note: Better: less sick than before. Weak: not strong. Still: it hasn't changed.
Take medicine. Not: eat or drink medicine.
Once a day, twice a day, three times a day. A meal: breakfast, lunch or dinner.

lines.text: Good. Can you do the dishes?
lines.note: Do the dishes: wash the plates, cups and pans.
Dizzy: everything seems to turn around you.

lines.text: Too bad. Paul called. Football at four.
lines.note: Too bad = that's a pity. Football: soccer, in American English.
= half past three, 3:30.

lines.text: It's a miracle. I feel much better.
lines.note: A miracle: a wonderful thing nobody can explain. Much better: a lot better.

lines.text: Wonderful. The dishes take twenty minutes.
lines.note: Take + time: how long something needs.

notes: Sickness takes a: I have a cold, a fever, a cough, a headache, a sore throat, a runny nose.
Feeling: I don't feel well, I feel dizzy, I feel weak, I feel a little better, I feel much better.
Pain: my back hurts, my leg hurts. Or with -ache: a headache, a stomachache, a toothache.
Advice: you should + verb. You should lie down. You should see a doctor. Softer: Have you tried drinking water?
Medicine: take your medicine once a day, twice a day, three times a day, after meals.
Temperature: 37.2 is thirty-seven point two. In Celsius, about 37 is normal and 38 is a fever.

questions.q: Lucas has a temperature of 37.2. What does Emma think?
questions.why: 37.2 is normal. Emma says: That's not a fever. That's a person.

questions.q: Emma has a headache. What is Lucas's advice?
options: Lie down in a quiet room.
questions.why: You should lie down in a quiet room. The doctor is for his back.
Something heavy… a sock. It was wet.

questions.q: When does Lucas take his medicine?
Why does Lucas suddenly feel much better?
questions.why: Paul called: football at four. The miracle comes right after.
